statusText: Tail risk low at 11%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 closed 6 October at a record 31,224.47 after granting a full retracement from its 31,361.37 intraday record, and the reopened globex session is observed holding a 25-point range at 31,511.75. Stress remains elevated at 45% on a long end near 24-year highs and Brent near $100.6.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 14 points below the block threshold, supported by an observed full retracement off the record high, a VIX session low of 15.01 and an orderly narrow globex range. A danger window is declared for 17:00-19:00Z on 7 October covering the 10-year note auction and the September FOMC minutes, where an aligned rates-and-equity repricing is the credible multi-stage mechanism. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its record 31,224.47 close and NQ trades a 25-point globex band at 31,511.75; Tail eases to 11% with the FOMC minutes danger window set for 7 October
body:
The 6 October US cash session closed with the Nasdaq-100 at a record 31,224.47, up 148.03 points or 0.48%, after setting a 31,361.37 record intraday high. The decisive observation for this hour is what happened after that high: price finished 0.44% below it and only 16.27 points above the 31,208.20 session low, so the retracement was granted and then extended into the bell. That is the signature of functioning mean reversion rather than of a pathological no-retracement path, which is why Tail eases to 11% even with the index at an all-time high.

Globex has since reopened after the 21:00Z maintenance halt and the post-halt evidence reinforces that read. NQ December futures are observed at 31,511.75, up 28.50 points or 0.09%, inside a 31,496.00-31,521.00 band - a 25-point range that is about as compressed as this contract trades. There is no observed directional efficiency, no repeated extension and no holding of a session extreme. VIX closed at 15.01, down 3.29% and at its own session low, so implied volatility is decaying alongside the orderly price path. The session low still held 0.42% above Monday's 31,076.44 record close, leaving the gap above the prior record unfilled and the daily uptrend structurally intact, which is why the dominant mode is read as mixed rather than trend-up.

The cross-asset backdrop is the reason Stress stays elevated at 45% while Tail sits near its floor. Long-dated Treasury yields eased 2.7 basis points to 5.28% on the 10-year but only after touching fresh 24-year highs on Monday, and the H.15 release for 5 October carries the 2-year at 4.84% and the 10-year at 5.31%. Monday's 3-year auction cleared at its highest yield since 2006. Brent settled near $100.6 and WTI near $89.8, with resilient Middle East crude exports and a G7 emergency stockpile release containing an eight-month US-Iran conflict that has not produced fresh escalation or new market transmission. Soaring diesel costs and a global bond sell-off are live stressors that have not dented equity risk appetite: breadth of the advance was wide, with the S&P 500 at a record 7,818.93 and the Nasdaq Composite at a back-to-back record 27,599.79. Nvidia and AMD both set all-time highs, Nvidia's market capitalisation approached $6 trillion, and Marvell gained roughly 8% after raising FY2028 revenue guidance.

The forward risk is concentrated and scheduled rather than observed. Fed Logan speaks at 23:00Z into thin post-halt liquidity, which supports a modest 13% Tail bump for that hour only. The substantive stack is on 7 October: EIA crude inventories at 14:30Z, September Consumer Inflation Expectations at 15:00Z, a 10-year note auction at 17:00Z and the minutes of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting at 18:00Z. Because September carried a Summary of Economic Projections, those minutes should detail how the committee debated its remaining 2026 path, and a long end this close to 24-year highs makes the auction-plus-minutes sequence a credible multi-stage mechanism for an aligned rates-and-equity repricing with a delayed second leg. The danger window is therefore declared narrowly for 17:00-19:00Z rather than across the whole session, and the forecast peak of 23% is deliberately held inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold, because it rests on scheduled event exposure and not on any observed one-way structure. Shared Finviz context was read but is dated 29 September with partial collection status, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness contract and was not used as evidence; this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment, so the window is complete. Tail opened at 11% at 22:00Z on 5 October, drifted to an 8% trough at 05:00Z as the index mean-reverted in thin Asian liquidity, then rebuilt through the European and US sessions to a 22% peak at 15:00Z on 6 October around the record-high push - the only hour of the window that entered the watch band, alongside 20% at 16:00Z. It fell back to 17-19% through the afternoon as the retracement off the 31,361.37 high was granted, then closed the window at 14% and 13% for the cash-close and post-close hours. Stress held a narrow 45-48% band throughout, never leaving the elevated bracket, and Confidence ran 86-88% on consistently available price-path evidence. Dominant mode read mixed overnight, shifted to trend-up from 10:00Z through the record-high push, and returned to mixed once the retracement was granted.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to ease through the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins, reaching a 9% trough between 03:00Z and 05:00Z, with a modest 13% bump at 23:00Z for the Fed Logan speech because a hawkish tone in thin liquidity is a plausible air pocket. It rebuilds with the European open and the US pre-market, then steps up into the 7 October US session: 18% for the 13:00Z cash-open hour, 19% through the EIA crude release, 20% as Consumer Inflation Expectations print at 15:00Z and the watch band is entered, 22% for the 17:00Z 10-year note auction and a 23% peak in the 18:00Z FOMC minutes hour. That peak stays inside the watch band and below the 25% block threshold because it rests on a scheduled multi-stage event rather than on observed one-way structure. Tail then falls back to 21% for the delayed-second-leg hour, 18% through the power hour and 14% at the cash close. Stress tracks the same shape more steeply, from 44% overnight to a 54% peak in the minutes hour, while Confidence decays from 87% to 79% as the slots move further from observed evidence. The declared danger window covers 17:00-19:00Z on 7 October.
